ask.text: It’s 2023. An employee asks the company’s new AI assistant, an LLM, about a customer contract.

era-origins.text: Confident, and wrong. A model knows only its training data plus its prompt, and it never saw your contracts.

era-small-windows.text: 2020: researchers named the fix. Fetch relevant text first, then let the model answer from it: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG.

era-retrieval-matures.text: 2023: companies rolled out chat assistants with context windows of 4.1K–200K tokens. Tool calling was new, so retrieval picked the paragraphs.

era-agents.text: 2024: Gemini 1.5 Pro’s window hit 2M tokens, the record. Retrieval got smarter: graphs, better chunks, reranking. Multi-step tool use still stumbled.

quiz.text: Late 2024–26: 1M-token windows became common (Llama 4 Scout claims 10M). Models now act as agents, and retrieval is one tool they choose. Last question.

predict.text: Your team’s obvious fix: paste the whole company drive into the assistant’s prompt. Before you try it, make a prediction.

ask.text: Your pick is locked. The drive is pasted in.

overflow.text: Wrong again. The policy is on the drive, but truncation cut the paste before it.

scale.text: It already overflows at 50 MB. Real company drives are much bigger.

reason-middle.text: 5 TB is about 1.25T tokens. No model reads that in one go, and size is only one problem.

reason-fresh.text: Even text that fits gets used badly: facts lost in the middle of a long prompt are often missed.

reason-access.text: A prompt is a snapshot. Documents change every day.

quiz.text: And one prompt for everyone ignores permissions. Retrieval can filter per user. One question to finish.

ask.text: Meet the assistant: for now just an LLM, with no documents wired in. A support lead asks it about refunds.

docs.text: Made up. It sounds sure, but it has never read your refund policy, so it invented one.

predict.text: Still made up: the documents are there, but nothing carries the right ones to the model. A Retriever finds the passages that match. Predict first.

grounded.text: Correct, and it cites the policy it used: a grounded answer. That is RAG: Retrieve the passages, Augment the prompt, Generate the answer.

math.text: These passages reached the model, each with a similarity score.

quiz.text: The retriever compares the meaning of your question with every passage and keeps the closest. One question to finish.

ask.text: The team now cuts documents into 16-word chunks and sends only the best.

predict.text: Wrong, and sure of itself. The policy excludes enterprise contracts, but only one 16-word chunk reached the model. Predict what it held.

chunker.text: Your pick is locked. Open up the pipeline. First layer: the Chunker cuts every document into chunks before any search.

embedder.text: There it is: a cut after “does NOT”, the red mark. The rule and its exception landed in different chunks.

map.text: The Embedder turns each chunk into an embedding, 384 numbers for its meaning; the vector index stores them.

assembler.text: The map is a picture; ranking uses the true score. Last layer: the Context assembler packs chunks into the prompt.

fix.text: Puzzle: the chunk the model gets ends on “does NOT”. Overlap repeats each chunk’s end in the next.

quiz.text: Correct, with a citation. With overlap the whole sentence sits in one chunk, so the model reads the exception. One question to finish.

ask.text: Your pipeline from the last chapter is live. A consultant booking a trip asks the assistant about the hotel limit.

evaluator.text: Wrong: $150 is from the retired 2018 travel policy. Before fixing anything, measure. The Evaluator judges the answer beside a retrieval meter.

predict.text: Two meters. Recall@k: did the right sentence reach the model? Answer: was the reply right? Recall is 0%. Predict what fetching more will do.

filter.text: Recall hit 100%, yet the answer is still wrong: the retired 2018 policy came along.

add-rewrite.text: Correct, citing the 2025 policy. Filters act before ranking, so stale text never competes.

rewrite.text: Puzzle: a warehouse lead types “it’s broken again, who do I even call?”. Nothing in the documents reads like that.

after-rewrite.text: Correct. The rewrite names a Portal outage outside business hours, so the Duty Desk rule ranks in: recall went 0% to 100%.

topk.text: Puzzle: top-k is how many chunks the retriever hands over. At 1, the dock-door safety rule never arrives.

add-reranker.text: Past 6, recall stays 100% but the answer turns NOT FOUND. The model loses facts in the middle of long context.

needle.text: Puzzle: a teammate set top-k to 10 “to be safe”, burying the rule mid-context.

after-needle.text: Correct, and recall never moved: the rule was retrieved all along, only its position changed.

distractor.text: Puzzle: asked how long card data is kept, the assistant quotes a look-alike note about demo data.

after-distractor.text: Correct. Keyword matching rewards the real policy’s exact terms, so it outranks the look-alike.

overlap.text: Puzzle: the refund-window sentence is sliced in two, so the model finds no clear answer.

after-overlap.text: Correct. Overlap repeats each chunk’s end at the start of the next, so a sentence near a cut survives whole.

strategy.text: Puzzle, the last one: only one chunk is sent, and the fixed-size chunker cuts the lodging rule mid-sentence.

quiz.text: Correct. Seven levers, and the two meters told you which side to fix. One question to finish.

recap.text: Every pipeline so far searched once: naive RAG, then advanced. Here the retriever sends one 16-word chunk, so each type’s strengths show.

naive-run.text: Each run adds a row to the results strip under the canvas.

attach.text: Wrong: one chunk stopped after “does NOT”. Agentic RAG puts an agent between retriever and model to decide whether to search again.

agent-run.text: The agent sits in the side bay, wired to the retriever both ways. Max calls caps its retrievals.

cost.text: Correct in 2 calls: the first chunk was cut mid-sentence, so the agent fetched its neighbours.

quiz.text: Both wrong, and the agent paid for a second search. Searching more never removes the retired 2018 policy: a metadata filter does. One question.

multi-hop.text: Harder: who approves purchases for the team owning the Kestrel K2 scanner integration? It spans two documents.

attach-graph.text: Not found either way: no single sentence links the scanner to the approver. GraphRAG walks a knowledge graph drawn from the documents.

graph-one.text: The graph starts from what your question names, the Kestrel K2, and follows relations outward to the sentences behind them.

graph-two.text: Still not found. One hop reached Fulfillment Systems, the team that owns the integration, and stopped short of its approver.

graph-quiz.text: Correct: the second hop reached Tomasz Rehnquist in another document. The price: the walk sent about two dozen chunks instead of one. One question.

sc-run.text: Next, a trap: how long does Larkspur keep customer payment card data? A meeting note about fake demo cards uses near-identical words.

sc-attach.text: Wrong: it read the demo note. Self-correcting RAG grades retrieval before answering, retries, and says “I don’t know” if nothing passes.

sc-grade.text: The Evaluator scores each search with a cross-encoder, which reads question and chunk together. A best chunk of 6 or more passes.

mm-attach.text: The look-alike and a rewrite both failed the bar, so it said “I don’t know”. No grade reads tables, PDFs or images.

mm-run.text: A plain-text reader skips tables and images, so the Docs block’s three parsers start off.

mm-tables.text: Not found: the price list is a table, and with table parsing off retrieval never sees it.

mm-more.text: Correct: $410, from the table’s K2 row. The sensor warranty sits in a vendor PDF, the lead in an org chart image.

open.text: Every block from chapters 3 to 6 is here, wired; the graph answers the module’s hardest question.

play.text: Now it is yours: drag blocks, wire them from their yellow knobs, click a wire to cut it.

challenge.text: Last stop. Five teams at Larkspur each describe a problem. Pick the RAG type that fits each one best.
